claims.claim: In the fed-state condition, ziprasidone reached approximately 59-60% absolute oral bioavailability when dosed after a high-fat meal, showing that a lipophilic, poorly water-soluble drug can meet the F>=20% threshold in the fed state.

Sertindole, another lipophilic antipsychotic, has approximately 74-75% oral bioavailability and L1 records report little food effect; L2 mostly reinforces this with tablet/solution relative bioavailability almost unity and no meal effect, although one L2 record states absorption is significantly affected by food/antacids.

New L2 records for other reference contexts predominantly report F above 20% (asciminib mouse 53%, apixaban rat/dog 30/70%, difloxacin 54-96%, rizatriptan ~40-45%, compound 26 dog 24%), supporting that high lipophilicity and neutral character do not preclude F>=20%.

The negative food-effect record for asciminib (exposure decreased ~65% with a high-fat meal) and the rat F=19% records for compound 26 are context/species-specific and do not establish F<20% for the query; the human predicted F for compound 26 is 23% and dog F is 24%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral-bioavailability record for the query molecule (an itraconazole-type azole) is present in the supplied cards.
No measured solubility, permeability, or first-pass data for the query are supplied; the low prior is physicochemical only.
The fed-state effect for the query is inferred from ziprasidone high-fat-meal and sertindole food-effect records rather than measured in the query.

Some L2 records report species-specific low F values (penicillin V in horses/foals/monkeys, compound 26 in rats) and a negative food effect for asciminib; their transferability to the query is uncertain.
The exact formulation and dose for the query are not specified, and fed-state bioavailability can be formulation-dependent.
content.decision_summary: Although the physicochemical prior is unfavorable, the fed-state ziprasidone records (~59-60% absolute F after a high-fat meal) and sertindole records (~74-75%, largely food-insensitive) support that this lipophilic azole can meet the F>=20% threshold; new L2 records predominantly reinforce F>=20% across related contexts, while the negative food-effect and species-specific low-F records are not transferable enough to overturn the prediction. Predict high with moderate confidence.

You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,

votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
